recipes.name: Backpack Recipes inspired by Marvel's Spider-Man
ingredients: 2 tbsp Chinese chives (or regular chives if you can’t find them)
instructions: In a large bowl combine the whole wheat flour with the sifted buckwheat flour, add the baking powder, baking soda, and salt. - 1 cup whole wheat flour - 1 cup buckwheat flour sifted - 2 tsp baking powder - 1 tsp baking soda - 1 tsp salt
In a separate bowl combine the buttermilk with the molasses. Whisk to combine and set aside. - 2 cups buttermilk - 2 tsp molasses
Whip your egg whites until they are stiff but not dry. Set aside. - 2 egg whites whipped
Add the beaten egg yolks to the dry mixture along with the wet mixture and melted butter. Mix to combine, but don’t over mix! (It’s okay if it’s lumpy) - 2 egg yolks beaten - ¼ cup melted butter
Fold in your whipped egg whites to create a fluffy batter. - 2 egg whites whipped

In a skillet heat up some bacon grease until pan is shimmering over a medium low heat. Add a nice amount of batter and flip when bubbles form on the surface and the bottom is browned and crisp. Cook the other side, and place on a plate when finished. Add butter and maple syrup. - Bacon grease - melted butter - Maple syrup

Combine all ingredients together in a bowl and whisk to combine and set aside - ½ cup soy sauce - 1 tbsp seasoned rice vinegar - 2 tbsp Chinese chives (or regular chives if you can’t find them) - Fresh garlic minced - 1 tbsp sesame seeds - 1 tbsp chili garlic sauce

In a large bowl combine the ground pork with the minced garlic cloves, the beaten egg, the Chinese chives, soy sauce, sesame oil, and the freshly minced ginger. Mix thoroughly to combine. - 1 pound of ground pork - 3 cloves large garlic minced - 1 egg beaten - 2 tbsp Chinese chives finely minced - 2 tbsp soy sauce - 2 tbsp sesame oil - 1 tbsp fresh ginger minced
Lightly dust your work surface with flour. Fill a small bowl with water and set aside. This will help seal the dumplings. - All purpose flour

Dip your finger in the water and gently wet the edge of the dumpling wrapper. Once the whole outside edge is wet, add about 1 tsp of your pork mixture to the center of the dumpling. Fold the wrapper in half, pinch where sides meet, wet the outside of the wrapper, and make 3 pleats on each side of the dumpling to seal it shut. (To see how to seal dumplings, click on the link in the description) - Dumpling wrappers
Heat up some vegetable oil in a nonstick pan over a medium high heat and cook on the bottom side until dumplings are lovely and browned. - Vegetable oil
Add the water to the hot pan, lower the heat to medium low, cover and let steam and cook for about 5 minutes. - ½ cup water
Remove from heat, let cool and serve with dumpling dipping sauce. - For The MJ’s Dumplings - For The Dipping Sauce
